The program finds every assignment of the form `name <- expression;` in the input. It evaluates each one in order, treating `mod` as Python's `%`. Before evaluating, it checks that the expression contains only names, numbers, arithmetic operators and parentheses.

```python
import sys
import re

def main():
    text = sys.stdin.read()
    env = {}
    pattern = re.compile(r'([A-Za-z_]\w*)\s*<-\s*([^;]+?)\s*;')
    safe = re.compile(r'^[\sA-Za-z_0-9+\-*/()%]*$')
    for m in pattern.finditer(text):
        name = m.group(1)
        expr = m.group(2)
        expr_py = re.sub(r'\bmod\b', '%', expr)
        if not safe.match(expr_py):
            continue
        try:
            val = eval(expr_py, {"__builtins__": {}}, dict(env))
        except Exception:
            continue
        env[name] = val
    out = []
    for v in ("a", "b", "TMP"):
        out.append(f"{v} ?= {env.get(v, 0)};")
    print(" ".join(out))

if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
```
